module.title: Coaching Conversations — Phát triển con người qua GROW model
module.focus: Học cách coach team members qua GROW model, active listening, powerful questioning, và DISC-based coaching để accelerate growth của từng người
module.overview: Module này dạy Chiến Binh kỹ năng COACHING — nghệ thuật giúp người khác tự tìm ra câu trả lời thay vì bạn tell họ phải làm gì. Coaching là skill #1 của leader. Leader mà không biết coaching = chỉ là manager. Manager command, coach empower. Trong M8, bạn sẽ master GROW model (Goal, Reality, Options, Will), active listening, powerful questioning, và DISC-based coaching style.
objectives: Hiểu coaching vs managing: khi nào dùng approach nào
Practice active listening: nghe để hiểu, không phải nghe để trả lời
Develop powerful questioning skills: câu hỏi mở thay vì closed questions
Apply DISC-based coaching: adapt style theo personality của coachee
Design và run buddy system coaching sessions
Build peer accountability framework cho PSN
Practice full GROW coaching cycle với team members
prerequisites: M7 PSN Management — PSN đã có 5+ members
Willingness to invest thời gian vào 1:1 coaching sessions

coaching_philosophy.definition: Coaching là process giúp person A (coachee) tự discover insights, make decisions, và take action — thông qua guided conversation với person B (coach). Coach KHÔNG tell coachee phải làm gì. Coach tạo space để coachee tự tìm ra answer.

managing.questions: Here's what you need to do

when_to_coach: Member có potential nhưng chưa realize it
Member đang face a challenge và cần find own solution
Member shows motivation nhưng unclear về direction
Performance issue mà training alone doesn't fix
Career development discussion: where do they want to go?
when_to_manage: Crisis situation: cần immediate action, không có time cho discussion
Clear instruction needed: task có rõ ràng what/how/when
Compliance issue: rules must be followed, no negotiation
New member onboarding: first 2 weeks cần clear guidance
Emergency: system down, order urgent, customer complaint
coaching_philosophy.coaching_balance: Great leaders coach 70% và manage 30%. If you're always managing, you're not developing people. If you're always coaching, nothing gets done. Find the balance.

grow_model.origin: Developed by Sir John Whitmore, GROW là coaching framework phổ biến nhất thế giới, used bởi Fortune 500 companies, Olympic coaches, và business leaders globally.

G.name: Goal
G.purpose: Xác định rõ coachee muốn đạt được gì
questions: What do you want to achieve?
What does success look like?
By when do you want to achieve this?
How will you know when you've achieved it?
On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you to this goal?
What's stopping you from being at 10?
G.quality_check: SMART + meaningful. If goal isn't specific, measurable, or meaningful to coachee, keep digging.

R.name: Reality
R.purpose: Hiểu rõ tình hình hiện tại của coachee
questions: Where are you now in relation to this goal?
What have you already tried?
What worked? What didn't?
What resources do you have?
What obstacles are in your way?
Who can help you?
R.quality_check: Factual, not judgmental. Coachee might blame external factors — gently bring them back to what THEY can control.

O.name: Options
O.purpose: Brainstorm cách thức để reach goal
questions: What are all the possible ways to achieve this?
What would you do if you had unlimited resources?
What would you advise a friend in this situation?
What's the craziest option? (sometimes crazy leads to creative)
What have you seen others do successfully?
If you say YES to this, what do you have to say NO to?
O.quality_check: Quantity > Quality at this stage. Don't judge ideas. Even 'bad' ideas can spark great ones.

W.name: Will
W.purpose: Commitment — coachee commits to specific actions
questions: Which option will you choose?
What specific action will you take?
By when?
What might get in your way?
How will you overcome that obstacle?
On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you?
What's your first step — right now?
W.quality_check: Action must be specific, time-bound, and coachee-owned. If commitment < 8/10, go back to Options.

active_listening.definition: Active listening = nghe với toàn bộ attention, không chỉ đợi đến lượt nói. 80% listening, 20% speaking. Most people listen 50% và think về what to say next.

level_1.name: Nghe bề mặt
level_1.description: Nghe từng từ, không connect ý
level_1.sign: Gật đầu trong khi đang nghĩ về việc trả lời

level_2.name: Nghe nội dung
level_2.sign: Có thể paraphrase lại những gì người kia nói

level_3.name: Nghe cảm xúc
level_3.description: Nhận ra emotions phía sau lời nói
level_3.sign: Cảm nhận được frustration, excitement, fear, hope dù người kia không nói trực tiếp

level_4.name: Nghe sâu (Active Listening)
level_4.description: Toàn bộ being present, reflect feelings, ask clarifying questions
level_4.sign: Coachee cảm thấy được TRULY heard, không chỉ được lắng nghe

techniques.name: Paraphrasing
techniques.description: Repeat coachee's words bằng cách của bạn để confirm understanding
techniques.example:
Coachee: 'Tôi cảm thấy overwhelmed, quá nhiều thứ cần làm.'
Coach: 'Vậy là bạn đang cảm thấy quá tải vì workload hiện tại, đúng không?'

techniques.name: Reflecting feelings
techniques.description: Reflect the emotion phía sau lời nói
techniques.example:
Coachee: 'Tôi đã thử mọi cách mà vẫn không recruit được ai.'
Coach: 'Nghe bạn nói, tôi cảm thấy có chút frustration. Đó có đúng không?'

techniques.name: Clarifying questions
techniques.description: Ask questions để make sure you understand
techniques.example: 'Khi bạn nói overwhelmed, cụ thể là phần nào trong công việc khiến bạn cảm thấy vậy?'

techniques.name: Summarizing
techniques.description: Summarize main points cuối cùng để confirm
techniques.example: 'Okay, let me summarize what I heard. Mục tiêu của bạn là X. Hiện tại bạn đang ở Y. Options bạn đã liệt kê là A, B, C. Bạn sẽ commit to action A trong 1 tuần. Đúng không?'

techniques.name: Silence
techniques.description: Let silence do the work. After asking a deep question, WAIT.
techniques.example: Coach asks: 'What do you REALLY want?' → Silence 5-10 seconds → Coachee often comes up with deeper answer

barriers_to_active_listening: Thinking about what to say next
Listening to respond, not to understand

powerful_questioning.definition: Câu hỏi mở (open-ended) tạo insights. Câu hỏi đóng (closed-ended) chỉ get facts. Coaching cần câu hỏi mở.

open_questions.description: Cannot be answered with yes/no. Force elaboration.
examples: What's important about this goal to you?
How do you feel about the current situation?
What would you do if you weren't afraid?
What's the real challenge here for you?
What would your ideal outcome look like?
open_questions.power: Unlock thinking, reveal values, generate options

closed_questions.description: Answered with yes/no or single word.
examples: Did you complete your connects today?
Do you want to recruit this month?
closed_questions.use: Clarify facts, confirm decisions, close discussions

miracle_questions.description: Hypothetical scenario that bypasses limiting beliefs.
examples: If a miracle happened tonight and this problem was solved, what would be different tomorrow?
If you had all the resources you needed, what would you do differently?
If you knew you couldn't fail, what would you try?
miracle_questions.power: Reveal true desires beyond self-imposed limitations

examples: On a scale of 1-10, how confident are you?
If 10 is your goal achieved, where are you now?
What would take you from a 6 to a 7?

loop_questions.description: Repeat coachee's own words back to deepen insight.
examples: You said 'overwhelmed' twice — what does that tell you?
Earlier you mentioned X. How does that connect to your goal?
You said this was 'important'. Important to whom?

questions_to_avoid: Why questions (feel interrogated): 'Why didn't you...?' → 'What happened when...?'
Leading questions (imply answer): 'Don't you think you should...?'
Advice disguised as questions: 'Have you tried doing X?' (unless they're stuck)
Questions about past that can't be changed (focus on future)

lessons.title: Coaching vs Managing — Sự khác biệt then chốt
lessons.objective: Hiểu rõ coaching và managing là gì, khi nào dùng cái nào, và tại sao coaching là skill #1 của leader
lessons.content:
Chào mừng đến Module 8 — Coaching Conversations! Module này sẽ thay đổi cách bạn lead team. Nếu M7 dạy bạn 'what to manage', M8 dạy bạn 'how to develop people'.

COACHING LÀ GÌ?

Coaching là một cuộc hội thoại có structure, giúp người khác tự discover answers thay vì bạn tell họ. Coach là facilitator, không phải expert.

METAPHOR:
- Manager = Người lái xe (drive)
- Coach = Người ngồi cạnh (help driver navigate)
- Coachee = Người lái xe thật sự (they drive, you guide)

Nếu bạn always drive, coachee never learns to drive. If you never drive (in crisis), car crashes.

THE COACHING SPECTRUM:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PURE COACHING ←→ BLENDED ←→ PURE MANAGING │
│   (Ask questions)  (Guide+Direct)  (Tell)   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Pure Coaching: Coachee owns every decision. Coach only asks questions.
→ Best for: Development, problem-solving, career growth
→ Example: 'What do you think is the best way to approach this recruitment challenge?'

Blended: Coach guides + provides input when needed.
→ Best for: Most leadership situations
→ Example: 'What's your plan? [wait] I've seen team X do Y with good results — what do you think about that approach?'

Pure Managing: Leader tells, member follows.
→ Best for: Crisis, compliance, new member first 2 weeks
→ Example: 'Today you need to complete Module 3 và make 10 connects. Here's exactly how.'

COACHING vs MANAGING — DETAILED COMPARISON:

| Dimension | Managing | Coaching |
|-----------|----------|----------|
| Mindset | 'Tôi biết best' | 'Bạn có thể tìm ra answer' |
| Focus | Tasks + results | Person + growth |
| Power | Leader holds | Coachee owns |
| Questions | 'Have you done X?' | 'What do you want to achieve?' |
| Feedback | Corrective (what's wrong) | Developmental (what's possible) |
| Timeframe | This week | This year |
| Outcome | Task completed | Person transformed |

WHY COACHING IS SKILL #1:

1. SCALABILITY: Manager fixes 1 problem. Coach develops 1 person who can fix infinite problems.

2. ENGAGEMENT: Coached members stay 3x longer, perform 2x better.
Research: Gallup found employees with a coach/mentor are 3x more engaged.

3. CULTURE: Coaching culture = psychological safety = innovation + retention.

4. LEADERSHIP PIPELINE: Every great leader was once coached. If you don't coach, no one will coach you when you're promoted.

5. SATISFACTION: Nothing more rewarding than watching someone transform from 'I can't' to 'I did it'.

THE 70/30 RULE:

70% Coaching (developing people)
30% Managing (getting things done)

If you're managing more than 30% of time, your team isn't growing. If you're coaching more than 70% and nothing gets done, you're not leading — you're therapisting.

Action items:
1. Audit last week: what % was coaching vs managing?
2. Identify 1-2 members who would benefit most from a coaching conversation
3. Schedule first 30-min coaching session this week

lessons.title: GROW Model Overview — Framework coaching chuẩn vàng
lessons.objective: Master GROW model: 4 bước coaching structure dùng bởi top leaders globally
lessons.content:
GROW model là foundation của coaching. Nếu bạn chỉ học 1 thing trong M8, hãy học GROW. Nó works cho EVERY situation: performance issue, goal setting, career development, conflict resolution.

GROW = Goal → Reality → Options → Will

ORIGIN:
Sir John Whitmore developed GROW in 1980s cho performance coaching in sports. Today, it's the most widely used coaching framework in business — taught tại Harvard Business School, used bởi Google, McKinsey, và thousands of leaders.

FULL GROW SESSION STRUCTURE:

PHASE 0: CONTRACTING (5 min) — Setup

Trước khi bắt đầu GROW, establish the coaching contract:

1. Purpose: 'Today we're going to talk about [topic]. Is that okay?'
2. Duration: 'We have 30 minutes. Does that work?'
3. Confidentiality: 'Everything we discuss stays between us (unless safety concern).'
4. Outcome: 'By the end, what would make this conversation valuable for you?'

Contracting matters because:
- Coachee knows what to expect
- Coachee feels safe (confidentiality)
- Coachee defines success (their outcome, not yours)

PHASE 1: GOAL (5-10 min) — WHERE DO YOU WANT TO GO?

Goal questions:
- 'What do you want to achieve from this conversation?' (outcome)
- 'What would you like to have happen as a result?' (vision)
- 'If we successfully complete this session, what will be different?' (success criteria)
- 'On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you to making this happen?' (commitment check)

Goal quality checks:
✅ SPECIFIC: 'Recruit 3 members this month' not 'recruit more'
✅ MEASURABLE: '10 connects/day' not 'connect more'
✅ MEANINGFUL: Must matter to COACHEE, not just you
✅ TIME-BOUND: 'By end of this month' not 'soon'

If goal is vague: keep asking until it's clear. 'What specifically?', 'How will you know?', 'By when?'

PHASE 2: REALITY (5-10 min) — WHERE ARE YOU NOW?

Reality questions:
- 'Where are you now in relation to this goal?' (baseline)
- 'What have you already tried?' (past actions)
- 'What worked? What didn't?' (lessons learned)
- 'What's currently in your way?' (obstacles)
- 'What resources do you have available?' (strengths)
- 'Who could help you?' (support network)

Reality principles:
- Stay factual, not judgmental. 'You've made 5 connects/day' not 'You're not trying hard enough'
- Acknowledge effort, not just results. 'I see you've been consistent with habits — that's the foundation'
- Surface hidden obstacles. 'Is there something else going on that's making this harder?'

PHASE 3: OPTIONS (10-15 min) — WHAT ARE YOUR CHOICES?

Options questions:
- 'What are ALL the possible ways to achieve this?' (brainstorm)
- 'If you had unlimited time/money/support, what would you do?' (break constraints)
- 'What have you seen others do in this situation?' (benchmarking)
- 'What's the simplest thing you could do that would make the biggest difference?' (Pareto)
- 'If you couldn't fail, what would you try?' (remove fear)

Options principles:
- Quantity > Quality at this stage. Encourage MANY ideas.
- Don't judge ideas. Even 'bad' ideas spark good ones.
- Coachee generates options. You might suggest 1-2 if they're stuck, but let THEM think first.
- Ask: 'What else?' 3-5 times. First 3 answers are obvious. The 4th-5th are where gold is.

PHASE 4: WILL (5-10 min) — WHAT WILL YOU DO?

Will questions:
- 'Which option will you choose?' (decision)
- 'What specific action will you take?' (action)
- 'By when will you do it?' (deadline)
- 'On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you?' (commitment check)
- 'What might get in your way?' (anticipate obstacles)
- 'How will you overcome that?' (contingency plan)
- 'What's your first step — literally the next action?' (immediate next step)
- 'When will you do it?' (time-bound)

Will principles:
- Action must be specific and time-bound. 'I'll make 10 connects tomorrow by 8pm' not 'I'll try harder'
- If commitment < 8/10, loop back to Options. 'What would make this a 9 or 10?'
- End with a celebration: 'I'm proud of the clarity you've created today.'

GROW SESSION TEMPLATE:

=== GROW COACHING SESSION ===
Coach: [Your name]
Coachee: [Name]
Date: [Date]
Duration: 30 min

CONTRACTING:
- Topic: ___
- Outcome desired: ___

GOAL:
- Specific goal: ___
- Commitment: ___/10

REALITY:
- Current state: ___
- What's tried: ___
- Key obstacle: ___

OPTIONS:
1. ___
2. ___
3. ___
4. ___

WILL:
- Chosen option: ___
- Specific action: ___
- Deadline: ___
- Commitment: ___/10
- First step: ___

COACH NOTES:
- What went well: ___
- What to follow up on: ___
- Patterns observed: ___
=========

COMMON GROW MISTAKES:

❌ Jumping to solutions (skipping Options or Will)
❌ Telling instead of asking ('You should do X')
❌ Accepting vague goals ('I'll try harder')
❌ Rushing through phases (especially Goal — worth the time)
❌ Taking responsibility for coachee's action (not your job)
❌ Multiple sessions on same issue without progress (if 3 sessions same problem → manage, don't coach)

Action items:
1. Memorize GROW acronym và each phase's purpose
2. Practice Contracting before every coaching conversation
3. Schedule 3 GROW sessions this week với different team members

lessons.title: G — Setting Coaching Goals — Mục tiêu coaching hiệu quả
lessons.objective: Master Goal phase của GROW: xác định goals rõ ràng, meaningful, achievable
lessons.content:
Goal phase là foundation của GROW. Bad goal = wasted session. Great goal = transformation. 80% của coaching success depends on quality của goal.

3 TYPES OF GOALS IN COACHING:

1. OUTCOME GOALS (Kết quả)
- Focus: What you want to achieve
- Example: 'Tôi muốn recruit 3 members trong tháng này'
- Characteristics: Specific, measurable, time-bound
- Danger: Too much focus on outcome can cause anxiety

2. PROCESS GOALS (Quá trình)
- Focus: What you need to DO consistently
- Example: 'Tôi sẽ make 10 connects mỗi ngày, 6 ngày/tuần'
- Characteristics: Within your control, daily/weekly habits
- Power: Process goals → naturally lead to outcome goals

3. IDENTITY GOALS (Bản sắc)
- Focus: Who you want to BECOME
- Example: 'Tôi muốn trở thành leader mà people naturally follow'
- Characteristics: Long-term, values-based, transformational
- Power: Identity goals change behavior at deepest level

GOAL HIERARCHY:

Identity goals (1-2 năm) → Process goals (hàng ngày) → Outcome goals (hàng tháng)

VD: Nếu identity goal là 'Trở thành trusted health advisor trong cộng đồng':
→ Process: 'Mỗi ngày post 1 educational content, reply 10 comments'
→ Outcome: '1,000 followers, 50 customers, 10 recruits trong 6 tháng'

SMART+ GOAL FRAMEWORK (Coaching version):

Beyond SMART, add these for coaching:

S — SPECIFIC: Exact, not vague
'Mình sẽ recruit 3 members cho PSN' not 'tuyển thêm người'

M — MEASURABLE: Countable
'10 connects/day, 3 recruits/month' — có thể track

A — ACHIEVABLE: Stretching nhưng reachable
Base trên current performance: nếu hiện tại 1 recruit/month, target 3 = achievable stretch

R — RELEVANT: Phải connect với WHY của coachee
'Tôi muốn recruit 3 members để PSN đạt 20 người, tôi promote lên Leader cấp 2'

T — TIME-BOUND: Deadline cụ thể
'Before end of this month (June 30)' not 'soon'

+ E — EXCITING: Phải spark excitement
Nếu goal không làm coachee cảm thấy excited → không phải right goal

+ R — REVIEWABLE: Có check-in points
'Tuần 1: 1 recruit, Tuần 2: 1 recruit, Tuần 3: 1 recruit'

GOAL-SETTING CONVERSATION FLOW:

Step 1: OPEN
'Today I'd like to talk about your goals. What would you like to focus on?'

Step 2: EXPLORE
'What's important about that goal for you?' (connect to WHY)
'What will achieving this mean for you?' (vision)
'Who else benefits when you achieve this?' (stakeholders)

Step 3: CLARIFY
'So your goal is [repeat back]. Is that right?'
'What does success look like specifically?'
'How will you know you've achieved it?'

Step 4: CHECK COMMITMENT
'On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you to this?'
If < 8: 'What would make it an 8 or higher?'

Step 5: ALIGN WITH PSN
'How does this goal contribute to PSN?'
'What support do you need from me or the team?'

COMMON GOAL MISTAKES:

❌ Too many goals: 'Tôi muốn recruit, sell, train, và lead simultaneously'
→ Fix: Max 2-3 goals per coaching cycle. Focus beats breadth.

❌ Leader's goal disguised as coachee's: 'Tôi want you to recruit'
→ Fix: Ask 'What do YOU want?' until their answer surfaces

❌ Vague goals: 'Do better'
→ Fix: Drill down with 'Specifically what? How will you measure it?'

❌ Unrealistic goals: '10 recruits this week'
→ Fix: Base on current data. Stretch 20-30%, not 500%.

❌ Goals without WHY: 'Tôi phải recruit 3 members'
→ Fix: Always connect to personal motivation

WHEEL OF LIFE (for holistic goal setting):

Sometimes business goals aren't the real priority. Use Wheel of Life to discover:

8 areas: Business, Health, Family, Finance, Learning, Social, Spirituality, Fun
Coachee rates each 1-10. Lowest score = hidden priority.

VD: Business 9, Health 3, Family 4 → Maybe the reason they're not performing in business is because health/family needs aren't met.

Action items:
1. Practice writing SMART+ goals for 3 team members
2. Ask each team member to rate their Wheel of Life (share 3 lowest scores)
3. Identify any hidden priorities affecting PSN performance

lessons.title: R — Exploring Current Reality — Thấu hiểu tình huống thực tế
lessons.objective: Master Reality phase của GROW: diagnose current situation without judgment
lessons.content:
Reality phase đơn giản nhưng đòi hỏi discipline. Most coaches jump to solutions without truly understanding reality. If you don't know WHERE someone is, you can't help them get WHERE they want to go.

THE REALITY PRINCIPLE:

People live in stories, not facts. Coachee might say 'Tôi không thể recruit ai' (story). Reality might be 'Tôi đã approached 5 người, 2 đã từ chối, 2 chưa reply, 1 đang consider' (facts).

Coach's job: Help coachee separate STORY from REALITY.

Story = Interpretation (often negative, limiting)
Reality = Observable facts (neutral, measurable)

STORY vs REALITY EXAMPLES:

❌ Story: 'Tôi tệ ở recruitment'
✅ Reality: 'Tôi đã recruit 1 member trong 30 ngày. Target là 3. Mình đã approached 8 people. 2 said no, 3 không reply, 2 đang interested, 1 joined.'

❌ Story: 'PSN của tôi không grow được'
✅ Reality: 'PSN có 8 members, 1 tháng trước có 6. +2 members. Revenue: 15 triệu/tháng, target 20. Habit score avg: 62/100.'

❌ Story: 'Mọi người không respect tôi'
✅ Reality: 'Meeting attendance: 4/8 = 50%. Last week: 6/8 = 75%. 2 people đã cancel without reason. Zalo group activity: 2-3 messages/day (down from 5-7).'

REALITY QUESTIONS DEEP DIVE:

FACT-FINDING:
- 'What's the current situation?' (baseline)
- 'What have you tried so far?' (actions taken)
- 'What was the result of each attempt?' (outcomes)
- 'What's working? What's not working?' (assessment)
- 'What data do you have?' (evidence-based)

EMOTIONAL REALITY:
- 'How do you feel about where you are right now?' (emotional state)
- 'What's the hardest part?' (pain point)
- 'What would make this easier?' (need identification)
- 'What are you most proud of despite the challenges?' (strength finding)

OBSTACLE MAPPING:

Ask coachee to map obstacles:

Level 1: External (outside their control)
- Market conditions, competitor activities
- Family circumstances, health issues
- Company policy changes, product issues

Level 2: Internal (within their control but hard)
- Skill gaps, knowledge gaps
- Habit inconsistency, discipline issues
- Fear of rejection, self-doubt

Level 3: Self-imposed (entirely their creation)
- Perfectionism, procrastination
- Imposter syndrome, limiting beliefs
- 'I'm not good at recruiting' (story, not fact)

For each obstacle, ask: 'What CAN you control about this?'

RESOURCE INVENTORY:

Help coachee discover resources they didn't know they had:

INTERNAL RESOURCES:
- Skills: What are you good at? (even if unrelated)
- Experiences: What have you learned?
- Relationships: Who do you know that could help?
- Time: How do you actually spend your day?
- Energy: When are you most productive?

EXTERNAL RESOURCES:
- PSN members: Who can help?
- Upline: Who has solved this before?
- Company: What training/resources available?
- Tools: Droppii app, Zalo groups, Google Sheets

REALITY SESSION FLOW:

1. OPEN (2 min): 'Let's look at where you are now — no judgment, just facts.'

2. CURRENT STATE (5 min):
- 'Tell me about your current situation.'
- Listen, take notes, reflect back

3. PAST ATTEMPTS (5 min):
- 'What have you tried?'
- 'What worked? What didn't?'
- 'What did you learn?'

4. OBSTACLES (5 min):
- 'What's in your way?'
- Map internal vs external
- 'What can you control?'

5. RESOURCES (3 min):
- 'What resources do you have?'
- Often coachee underestimates their own resources

6. SUMMARY (2 min):
- 'Here's what I understand. [Summarize]. Is that accurate?'
- Confirm before moving to Options

COMMON REALITY PHASE MISTAKES:

❌ Judging: 'You should have tried harder' → kills openness
❌ Solving: Jumping to options before fully exploring reality
❌ Accepting first answer: 'It's fine' — dig deeper
❌ Focusing only on problems: also find what's working
❌ Letting them wallow: balance empathy with forward momentum

Action items:
1. Practice Reality phase with 1 team member this week
2. Help them separate 3 'stories' from 'facts' in their current situation
3. Create obstacle map for your own PSN challenge

lessons.title: O — Generating Options — Brainstorm giải pháp
lessons.objective: Master Options phase của GROW: generate diverse solutions without judgment
lessons.content:
Options phase là where magic happens. Most people stop at 2-3 ideas. Great coaches push to 10+ options. Why? Because the best solution is usually NOT the first one. Quantity leads to quality.

OPTIONS PHILOSOPHY:

The goal of Options phase is NOT to find THE solution. The goal is to expand possibility space. More options = more freedom = better decisions.

Bad Options session:
Coach: 'What could you do?'
Coachee: 'I don't know'
Coach: 'Hmm...'
Result: No progress, both frustrated

Great Options session:
Coach: 'What could you do?' (wait)
Coachee: 'Maybe I could...'
Coach: 'What ELSE?'
Coachee: 'Or I could...'
Coach: 'What ELSE?' (5+ times)
Coachee: 'Wait, I just thought of something crazy but...'
Coach: 'Tell me everything'
Result: 10+ options, coachee excited about multiple paths

OPTIONS GENERATION TECHNIQUES:

1. BRAINSTORM (No judgment):
'Write down EVERY idea, no matter how silly. We'll evaluate later, not now.'

2. CONSTRAINT REMOVAL:
'If you had unlimited time/money/support, what would you do?'
This reveals the IDEAL solution. Then work backwards: 'What CAN you do given your constraints?'

3. OPPOSITE THINKING:
'What's the OPPOSITE of what you've been doing?'
'If connecting before 8am isn't working, what about connecting during lunch?'

4. BEST PRACTICE BORROWING:
'What have you seen other successful leaders do?'
'What would [role model] do in this situation?'

5. WHAT WOULD X ADVISE:
'If your best friend had this problem, what would you tell them?'
People are often wiser about others' problems than their own.

6. MIRACLE QUESTION:
'If tonight a miracle happened and this problem was solved, what would be different tomorrow?'
Reveals the desired state beyond current constraints.

OPTION CATEGORIES:

Always generate options in these 4 categories:

1. PERSONAL ACTION (What can coachee do themselves?)
- 'I could wake up 1 hour earlier to connect before work'
- 'I could join a health group on Zalo and contribute daily'

2. TEAM ACTION (What can PSN/team do?)
- 'We could run a recruitment event this weekend'
- 'I could ask [Name] to be my accountability buddy'

3. SYSTEM ACTION (What process/structure changes?)
- 'I could create a connect tracking spreadsheet'
- 'PSN could implement daily standup calls'

4. MINDSET ACTION (What thinking/belief changes?)
- 'I could stop seeing rejection as failure'
- 'I could reframe connects as 'helping people' not 'selling'

OPTIONS EVALUATION (After generation):

Once you have 10+ options, evaluate:

For each option, rate:
1. IMPACT: How much will this move the needle? (1-10)
2. EFFORT: How hard is this to implement? (1-10, lower = easier)
3. CONTROL: How much is within coachee's control? (1-10)

SCORING = Impact × Control ÷ Effort
Highest score = best option to start with

DECISION FRAMEWORKS:

If coachee is stuck between 2 good options:

1. PRO-CON LIST (x3 each):
- List 3 pros, 3 cons for each option
- Rate each pro/con 1-5 for importance
- Add up — clear winner emerges

2. 10-10-10 TEST:
- How will I feel about this in 10 minutes?
- How will I feel in 10 months?
- How will I feel in 10 years?
- The option that feels best long-term usually wins

3. REGRET MINIMIZATION:
- 'Which option will I regret NOT taking?'
- 'At age 80, looking back, which choice would I be proud of?'

COACH'S ROLE IN OPTIONS:

DO:
- Encourage quantity: 'What ELSE?', 'And another one?'
- Build on their ideas: 'What if you combined X and Y?'
- Challenge assumptions: 'What makes you think that's not possible?'
- Celebrate creativity: 'That's a great idea!'

DON'T:
- Jump in with YOUR solution too early
- Dismiss 'silly' ideas (they spark better ideas)
- Pressure them to choose quickly
- Choose FOR them (they must own the decision)

COMMON OPTIONS PHASE MISTAKES:

❌ Coach provides solution: 'You should do X' → kills ownership
❌ First idea accepted: 'That's fine' → misses better options
❌ No wild ideas: Everything safe and conventional → no breakthrough
❌ Too many options: 20+ creates decision paralysis → cap at 8-10
❌ Rushing: 5 minutes for options → spend 10-15 min here

Action items:
1. Practice generating 10+ options for a common PSN challenge (e.g., low connects)
2. Use constraint removal technique: 'What if you had infinite time/money?'
3. Practice evaluating options with Impact × Control ÷ Effort formula

lessons.title: W — Building Commitment — Chuyển insights thành action
lessons.objective: Master Will phase của GROW: transform insights into committed action
lessons.content:
Will phase là where rubber meets road. Great goal, clear reality, many options — but if no action, the entire coaching session was wasted. Will = commitment to specific, time-bound action.

WILL = WANT + INTENTION + LOGIC + ENERGY

WANT: Does coachee truly want this?
INTENTION: Have they made a clear decision?
LOGIC: Do they have a realistic plan?
ENERGY: Are they excited and energized to act?

If all 4 are present → high commitment. If any missing → revisit earlier phases.

WILL PHASE STRUCTURE:

STEP 1: CHOOSE (Decision)
'Looking at all the options we discussed, which one resonates most with you?'
'What feels like the right next step?'
'If you had to pick ONE thing to do this week, what would it be?'

STEP 2: SPECIFY (Action detail)
'What exactly will you do?' (vague → specific)
Coachee: 'I'll connect more'
Coach: 'How many? When? How?'
Coachee: 'I'll make 15 connects tomorrow morning before work'

STEP 3: TIME-BIND (Deadline)
'When will you do this?'
'What's the exact time/day?'
'Is that realistic given your schedule?'

STEP 4: COMMIT (Scale 1-10)
'On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you to doing this?'
If < 8: 'What would make this an 8 or 9?'
If still < 8: This might not be the right action or right time.

STEP 5: ANTICIPATE OBSTACLES
'What might get in the way of you doing this?'
'How will you handle that when it comes up?'
'What's your backup plan?'

STEP 6: FIRST STEP (Micro-action)
'What's the very FIRST thing you need to do?'
'When will you do that first step?'
'Can you do it today?'

STEP 7: ACCOUNTABILITY
'How will you track this?'
'Who will you tell about this commitment?'
'When should we check in on this?'

WILL QUESTIONS MENU:

CHOICE:
- 'Which option will you choose?'
- 'What feels right for you?'
- 'If you could only pick one, which one?'

SPECIFICITY:
- 'What exactly will you do?'
- 'How many? How often? How long?'
- 'What does that look like in practice?'

TIMING:
- 'When will you start?'
- 'What day/time?'
- 'Is that realistic with your schedule?'

COMMITMENT:
- 'On a scale of 1-10?'
- 'What would make it higher?'
- 'Are you willing to commit to this?'

OBSTACLES:
- 'What might stop you?'
- 'How will you handle that?'
- 'What's your plan B?'

FIRST STEP:
- 'What's the very first action?'
- 'Can you do it today?'
- 'What do you need to get started?'

ACCOUNTABILITY:
- 'How will you track progress?'
- 'When should we check in?'
- 'Who else should know about this?'

ACCOUNTABILITY MECHANISMS:

1. COACH CHECK-IN:
- 'Let's schedule a 10-min check-in on [date]. I'll ask you how it went.'
- Coachee knows they'll be asked = more likely to follow through

2. PUBLIC COMMITMENT:
- 'Would you be willing to share this goal in our PSN group?'
- Public commitment increases follow-through by 65% (research)

3. ACCOUNTABILITY BUDDY:
- Pair coachee với another member for mutual accountability
- Weekly check-in between buddies

4. VISUAL TRACKER:
- Create visible progress tracker (calendar, spreadsheet, app)
- Every completed day = visual reinforcement

5. REWARD SYSTEM:
- 'What will you do to celebrate when you achieve this?'
- Small rewards for milestones, big reward for completion

WILL PHASE COMPLETION:

A complete Will section looks like:

✅ Specific action: 'Make 15 connects every morning before 8am, starting tomorrow'
✅ Deadline: 'For the next 14 days'
✅ Obstacle plan: 'If I oversleep, I'll do connects during lunch break'
✅ First step: 'Tonight, prepare my connect list of 20 prospects'
✅ Accountability: 'I'll report to you every Monday. I'll also tell Hùng.'
✅ Commitment: 9/10

Action items:
1. Complete Will phase for each of your 3 coaching sessions this week
2. Set up accountability check-in schedule với each coachee
3. Create simple progress tracker template cho team members

lessons.title: Week 1 Review — GROW Practice Reflection
lessons.objective: Review GROW model practice và identify areas for improvement
lessons.content:
Sau 6 ngày học GROW theory, đây là lúc review practice của bạn. Coaching là skill — chỉ improve through deliberate practice.

GROW FLUENCY CHECK:

Rate yourself 1-5 on each phase:

CONTRACTING (Setup):
- I establish clear purpose và outcome before starting
- I set expectations about confidentiality
- I confirm coachee's desired outcome
Score: ___/5

GOAL:
- I help coachee set specific, measurable goals
- I connect goals to personal WHY
- I check commitment level (1-10 scale)
- I push past vague answers to clarity
Score: ___/5

REALITY:
- I help coachee separate stories from facts
- I explore obstacles systematically
- I identify hidden resources
- I stay factual, not judgmental
Score: ___/5

OPTIONS:
- I generate 10+ options consistently
- I use multiple brainstorming techniques
- I don't jump to my own solutions
- I evaluate options with coachee
Score: ___/5

WILL:
- I help coachee make specific commitments
- I time-bound every action
- I set up accountability mechanisms
- I anticipate obstacles proactively
Score: ___/5

OVERALL GROW SCORE: ___/25
15-20: Solid GROW coach
20-25: Advanced — ready to coach complex situations

COMMON PITFALLS (Self-assessment):

Which of these have you done this week?

❌ Telling instead of asking: 'You should do X'
❌ Accepting vague goals: 'I'll try harder'
❌ Jumping to solutions: Before exploring Options fully
❌ Only 2-3 options generated: Not pushing for more
❌ Vague actions: 'I'll do better'
❌ No accountability: No follow-up scheduled
❌ Coach-centric: Making it about your agenda, not theirs
❌ Fixing: Trying to solve their problem instead of letting them

COACHING SESSION REVIEW:

For each session you conducted this week, ask:

1. What went well?
- Which phase felt most natural?
- Which question got the best response?
- What breakthrough did coachee have?

2. What was challenging?
- Which phase felt awkward?
- When did you want to jump in with advice?
- What question didn't work?

3. What would you do differently?
- If you could redo one session, what would change?
- Which technique would you practice more?

4. What did the coachee say?
- Did they feel heard?
- Did they leave with clear action?
- Would they want another session?

IMPROVEMENT PLAN:

Based on your self-assessment:

Weakest phase → Practice 2x this week
Strongest phase → Use it as foundation, help others with it
Common pitfall → Set up personal rule to prevent it

PRACTICE EXERCISES:

Exercise 1: GROW Role-Play (30 min)
- Pair with another leader
- Take turns being coach and coachee
- Use real PSN challenge as topic
- Debrief after: what worked, what didn't

Exercise 2: Question Bank Building
- Write 20 open-ended questions (5 per GROW phase)
- Keep them visible during sessions
- Add new ones as you discover them

Exercise 3: Silent Coach
- In next PSN meeting, practice ONLY asking questions
- No statements, no advice, no answers
- Just questions. See what happens.

Action items:

2. Identify your weakest GROW phase
3. Schedule practice role-play session với peer leader
4. Build your personal GROW question bank (20 questions)

lessons.title: Active Listening Skills — Nghệ thuật nghe thực sự
lessons.objective: Develop deep active listening skills — the foundation of all effective coaching
lessons.content:
Active listening là skill #0 của coaching. Without listening, coaching doesn't exist. Most people think they're good listeners. They're not. Average person listens at 25% efficiency — trong khi nghĩ về what to say next.

THE 4 LEVELS OF LISTENING:

LEVEL 1: Nghe từng từ
- Nghe nhưng không xử lý
- Miss the meaning behind words
- Can repeat what was said but didn't understand
- Like hearing noise vs hearing music

LEVEL 2: Nghe nội dung
- Process the meaning of sentences
- Can summarize what was said
- Like reading a book — get the plot
- But miss the subtext

LEVEL 3: Nghe cảm xúc
- Hear the emotion BEHIND the words
- Detect: frustration masked as 'I'm fine', excitement hidden in 'just okay', fear behind 'I don't know'
- Like watching a movie — feel the characters' emotions
- Most people stop here

LEVEL 4: Nghe sâu (Active Listening)
- Full presence: body, mind, and attention
- Reflect back what you hear
- Ask clarifying questions
- Let silence work
- Coachee feels TRULY understood
- Like being IN the movie — you experience it with them

ACTIVE LISTENING TECHNIQUES:

1. PARAPHRASING:
Repeat coachee's message bằng words của bạn để confirm understanding.

Formula: 'What I hear you saying is...' hoặc 'So if I understand correctly...'

Example:
Coachee: 'Tôi đã thử mọi cách rồi mà recruits vẫn không join. Tôi mệt mỏi quá.'
Coach: 'What I hear you saying is bạn đã put in a lot of effort but chưa thấy results, và điều đó khiến bạn feel frustrated và maybe questioning nên continue không.'
Coachee: 'Đúng rồi... tôi cũng không biết nên tiếp tục hay dừng lại.'

Why it works: Coachee feels heard. Often, being heard IS the solution.

2. REFLECTING FEELINGS:
Name the emotion you hear beneath the words.

Formula: 'It sounds like you're feeling...' hoặc 'I sense some ___ in what you're sharing'

Emotion words to use:
- Frustrated, discouraged, overwhelmed
- Excited, proud, energized
- Uncertain, hesitant, conflicted
- Grateful, inspired, motivated
- Anxious, worried, afraid

Example:
Coachee: 'Tuần này tôi chỉ recruit được 1 người, thấp hơn target.'
Coach: 'That sounds discouraging. You set a goal and came up short — that's tough.'
Coachee: 'Yeah... nhưng mà tôi vẫn thấy progress so với tháng trước.'
→ Coach opened door for coachee to find their own silver lining

3. CLARIFYING QUESTIONS:
Ask questions to dig deeper when something is unclear or interesting.

- 'What do you mean by ___?'
- 'Can you tell me more about ___?'
- 'When you say ___, what does that look like?'
- 'What's an example of that?'
- 'Walk me through a specific situation'

4. SUMMARIZING:
At key points, summarize what you've heard. This does 3 things:
- Confirms you understood correctly
- Helps coachee hear their own thinking
- Creates natural transition to next phase

Formula: 'So far, we've talked about [A], [B], and [C]. What I'm hearing is [insight]. Is that right?'

5. SILENCE:
Most powerful tool in coaching. After asking a deep question, WAIT.

Why silence works:
- Most people need 3-5 seconds to think
- First answer is often superficial
- Deeper answer comes after silence
- Silence creates psychological safety ('They're not rushing me')

How to use silence:
- After 'What's really important to you about this?' → Wait 5 seconds
- After coachee shares something emotional → Wait 3 seconds before responding
- After asking 'What else?' → Wait for them to think

Don't fill silence with your words. Let the silence do the work.

LISTENING BARRIERS — AND HOW TO OVERCOME:

BARRIER 1: Rehearsing your response
→ Fix: Focus entirely on their words. Take brief notes to stay engaged.

BARRIER 2: Filtering (only hearing what confirms your beliefs)
→ Fix: Listen to understand, not to confirm. Suspend judgment.

BARRIER 3: Advising (jumping to solutions)
→ Fix: Remind yourself: 'My job is to listen, not fix.'

BARRIER 4: Getting emotional
→ Fix: Notice your own emotions. Breathe. Stay present for them.

BARRIER 5: Pretending to listen
→ Fix: If you're distracted, be honest. 'I'm sorry, my mind wandered. Can you repeat that last part?'

LISTENING BODY LANGUAGE:

Even in Zalo/phone coaching, body language matters:
- Nod (even on video — they can see it)
- 'Mhm', 'I see', 'Tell me more' (verbal acknowledgment)
- Lean in slightly (shows engagement)
- Don't check phone/computer during session
- Maintain eye contact on video

Action items:
1. Practice paraphrasing in your next 1:1 conversation
2. Use silence intentionally: after next deep question, count to 5
3. Practice reflecting emotions: name what you hear beneath the words
4. Ask for feedback: 'Did you feel heard in our conversation?'

lessons.title: Powerful Questioning — Kỹ thuật hỏi đúng câu
lessons.objective: Develop powerful questioning skills — ask questions that unlock thinking and drive action
lessons.content:
Câu hỏi là tool mạnh nhất của coach. Một câu hỏi đúng có thể change perspective. Một câu hỏi sai có thể shut down conversation. Trong coaching, bạn are what you ask.

OPEN vs CLOSED QUESTIONS:

CLOSED: Yes/no answers. Get facts, stop conversation.
'Did you make your connects today?' 'Yes.' [Silence]
→ Good for: Closing, confirming, fact-checking

OPEN: Require elaboration. Spark thinking, extend conversation.
'What did you learn from today's connects?' → Thinking, sharing, insights
→ Good for: Coaching, exploring, developing

COACHING QUESTION ARCHETYPES:

1. AWAKENING QUESTIONS (Tạo nhận thức)
- 'What's really going on here?'
- 'What are you not saying?'
- 'If you were totally honest with yourself, what would you say?'
- 'What would you say if you couldn't lie?'
- 'What's the elephant in the room?'

2. PERSPECTIVE QUESTIONS (Đổi góc nhìn)
- 'How would you advise a friend in this situation?'
- 'If you were [role model], what would you do?'
- 'What would this look like from their perspective?'
- 'Six months from now, looking back, what would you want to have done?'
- 'If this was happening to someone else, what would you think?'

3. EXPLORATION QUESTIONS (Đào sâu)
- 'Tell me more about that'
- 'What else?' (most powerful — ask 3-5 times)
- 'What's behind that?'
- 'What does that mean for you?'
- 'Walk me through a typical day when this happens'
- 'What's the real challenge here?'

4. POSSIBILITY QUESTIONS (Mở ra lựa chọn)
- 'If you couldn't fail, what would you try?'
- 'What's possible here that you haven't considered?'
- 'What would need to be true for this to work?'
- 'If resources were unlimited, what would you do?'
- 'What's the boldest version of this idea?'

5. COMMITMENT QUESTIONS (Chuyển thành action)
- 'What will you do?'
- 'By when?'
- 'What's your first step?'
- 'On a scale of 1-10, how committed?'
- 'What will you do when [obstacle] happens?'

6. VALUES QUESTIONS (Kết nối với WHY)
- 'What's important to you about this?'
- 'What values are at stake here?'
- 'Why does this matter to you?'
- 'Who will benefit when you succeed?'
- 'What legacy do you want to create?'

THE 'WHAT ELSE?' TECHNIQUE:

The single most powerful questioning technique. After every answer, ask 'What else?'

Why it works:
- First answer is usually obvious/safe
- 2nd-3rd answer is more thoughtful
- 4th-5th answer is where insights live
- Coachee often says 'Wait, I never thought of that'

Example:
Coach: 'What options do you have to increase your connects?'
Coachee: 'I could wake up earlier.'
Coach: 'What else?'
Coachee: 'I could join more Zalo groups.'
Coach: 'What else?'
Coachee: 'I could ask my existing customers for referrals.'
Coach: 'What else?'
Coachee: 'I could... wait, actually I could do a connect challenge với my buddy.'
Coach: 'Tell me more about that.'

QUESTIONS TO AVOID:

❌ WHY questions (feel like interrogation)
'Why didn't you do your connects?' → 'What happened when you tried to do your connects?'
'Why are you behind?' → 'What do you think contributed to this?'

❌ LEADING questions (imply answer)
'Don't you think you should wake up earlier?' → 'What time of day works best for you?'
'Wouldn't it be better to...?' → 'What are your thoughts on...?'

❌ MULTIPLE questions (overwhelming)
'How's your connects going? Did you finish training? What about recruitment? How's your health?'
→ Ask ONE question at a time

❌ FUTURE questions about PAST (can't change it)
'Why didn't you... last week?' → 'What will you do differently this week?'

❌ QUESTIONS THAT CLOSE:
'So you'll do 10 connects tomorrow, right?' → 'What's your plan for tomorrow?'

POWERFUL QUESTION PRACTICE:

Build your question bank — 50 questions total:
- 10 Goal questions
- 10 Reality questions
- 10 Options questions
- 10 Will questions
- 10 General/Values questions

lessons.title: DISC-Based Coaching — Adapt style theo personality
lessons.objective: Apply DISC framework to coaching: adapt your coaching style to match coachee's personality
lessons.content:
Mỗi người học và nhận coaching KHÁC NHAU. D-type cần direct, challenges. S-type cần support, reassurance. C-type cần logic, evidence. I-type cần enthusiasm, variety. Nếu bạn dùng cùng một style với everyone, bạn'll miss 75% của people.

DISC RECAP — Coaching lens:

D — DOMINANCE (The Driver)
- Focus: Results, action, winning
- Pace: Fast, decisive
- Fear: Losing control, being perceived as weak
- Motivation: Challenge, competition, achievement

I — INFLUENCE (The Enthusiast)
- Focus: People, fun, recognition
- Pace: Fast, spontaneous
- Fear: Rejection, being ignored
- Motivation: Social connection, praise, excitement

S — STEADINESS (The Supporter)
- Focus: Stability, harmony, helping
- Pace: Slow, deliberate
- Fear: Change, conflict, losing security
- Motivation: Appreciation, belonging, steady progress

C — CONSCIENCE (The Analyst)
- Focus: Quality, accuracy, logic
- Pace: Slow, methodical
- Fear: Being wrong, criticism
- Motivation: Mastery, correctness, improvement

COACHING STYLE PER DISC TYPE:

COACHING D-TYPES:
Style: Direct, challenge-oriented, results-focused

✅ DO:
- Get straight to the point: 'Let's talk about your results. Here's what I see.'
- Challenge them: 'You're capable of more. Why aren't you there?'
- Set bold targets: 'I think you can do 20 connects/day'
- Give them autonomy: 'Here's the goal, you figure out how'
- Focus on outcomes, not process

❌ DON'T:
- Soft-pedal feedback (they want directness)
- Over-explain (they want bullet points)
- Micromanage process (they need freedom)
- Over-emotionalize (they want facts)

Coaching questions for D:
- 'What's the biggest challenge, and how are you going to overcome it?'
- 'If you were in charge, what would you change?'
- 'What would it take to double your results this month?'

COACHING I-TYPES:
Style: Enthusiastic, relational, fun

✅ DO:
- Start with connection: 'How are you doing? Tell me about your week!'
- Celebrate enthusiastically: 'That's AMAZING!'
- Use stories and examples
- Vary the format: don't make every session identical
- Include social elements: team events, group recognition

❌ DON'T:
- Be cold or robotic
- Stick to pure data without emotion
- Make sessions feel like reports
- Criticize in front of others

Coaching questions for I:
- 'What part of this excites you most?'
- 'Who can help you stay motivated?'
- 'How can we make this more fun?'

COACHING S-TYPES:
Style: Patient, supportive, relationship-first

✅ DO:
- Create safety: 'There's no pressure. Take your time.'
- Be patient: they need time to open up
- Provide clear, step-by-step guidance
- Acknowledge effort: 'I see how hard you're trying'
- Give advance notice: 'Next week we'll talk about X' — don't surprise them
- Be consistent: same time, same format, same coach

❌ DON'T:
- Rush them or push too hard
- Give harsh feedback publicly
- Change plans last minute
- Expect quick decisions

Coaching questions for S:
- 'What support do you need from me?'
- 'How can we make this feel safe and manageable?'
- 'What's one small step you could take this week?'

COACHING C-TYPES:
Style: Logical, systematic, quality-focused

✅ DO:
- Present data and evidence
- Show systematic approach: 'Here's a framework...'
- Give detailed, structured feedback
- Let them analyze: 'What patterns do you see?'
- Set precise, measurable targets
- Acknowledge accuracy and quality

❌ DON'T:
- Be vague or hand-wavy
- Push for fast decisions without data
- Ignore details they care about
- Make emotional appeals without logic

Coaching questions for C:
- 'What data supports your current approach?'
- 'What's the evidence that this is working?'
- 'What system could you create to improve this?'
- 'What would the perfect process look like?'

DISC COACHING DYNAMICS:

Coach D + Coachee D = Fast results, possible conflict
→ Coach: Be direct but DON'T compete. Set challenge, let them run.

Coach D + Coachee S = Impatient coach, overwhelmed coachee
→ Coach: Slow down. Create safety. Small steps, big patience.

Coach S + Coachee D = Underwhelming for D, perfect for S
→ Coach: Add urgency for D-types. Don't change yourself for D — adapt within your style.

Coach I + Coachee C = Missed details, frustrated analyst
→ Coach: Add structure, data, specifics. Don't just 'vibe' with C-types.

COACHING PITFALLS PER TYPE:

D-type coachee:
- Too much coaching = they'll quit (they want to DO, not talk)
- Keep sessions SHORT (20-30 min)
- Focus on action, not feelings

I-type coachee:
- They'll talk forever without action
- Time-box sessions: 'We have 25 minutes, let's make sure we end with action'
- Redirect tangents gently: 'That's great — how does this connect to your goal?'

S-type coachee:
- They'll say 'yes' to avoid conflict but not follow through
- Ask: 'On a scale of 1-10, how confident are you?' rather than 'Is this okay?'
- Check in BETWEEN sessions, not just during

C-type coachee:
- Analysis paralysis: can't decide because they want more data
- Set deadline: 'Let's decide by end of this session'
- Give them permission: 'Sometimes good enough is better than perfect'

Action items:
1. Identify DISC type of each team member
2. Adapt your coaching style for next 1:1 with each person
3. Practice coaching a D-type and an S-type differently this week

lessons.title: Buddy System Design — Hệ thống học việc nâng cao
lessons.objective: Design và implement enhanced buddy system với coaching structure
lessons.content:
Buddy system trong M7 là introduction. M8 nâng buddy system lên coaching level. Mỗi buddy session là một MINI coaching session — structured, purposeful, outcome-driven.

BUDDY SYSTEM v2 — OVERVIEW:

Purpose: Accelerate new member success through peer coaching
Structure: Senior member (buddy) coaches junior member (buddy) via weekly sessions
Duration: 20-30 phút/tuần
Format: Zalo call hoặc in-person
Outcome: New member reaches performance targets 2x faster

BUDDY SESSION STRUCTURE (30 min, coaching-based):

00:00-00:05 | CHECK-IN (5 min)
'How was your week? Wins? Challenges?'
- Listen actively, don't jump to solutions
- Celebrate any progress, however small

00:05-00:10 | HABIT REVIEW (5 min)
- Habit score: 'What was your average this week?'
- Connect activity: 'How many connects did you make?'
- Orders: 'Any orders this week?'
- Attendance: 'Did you attend the PSN meeting?'

00:10-00:25 | COACHING CONVERSATION (15 min) — The core
Use mini-GROW format:

G — Goal: 'What's one thing you want to improve this week?'
R — Reality: 'Where are you now with that?'
O — Options: 'What could you do differently?'
W — Will: 'What will you commit to?'

Keep it simple. New members don't need full 30-min GROW.

00:25-00:28 | ENCOURAGEMENT (3 min)
- Specific praise: 'I've noticed you've improved at ___. That's impressive.'
- Motivational push: 'You're doing great. Keep going.'
- Prayer/blessing if applicable

00:28-00:30 | CLOSE (2 min)
- 'See you next week. Same time?'
- Quick commitment confirmation: 'What's your one action for this week?'

BUDDY QUALIFICATIONS:

To be a buddy, a member should:
- 3+ months experience trong Droppii
- Consistent performer (top 50% of PSN)
- Patient and supportive personality (S or I-type preferred)
- Available: 30 min/week commitment
- Completed M8 Coaching module (or in progress)

BUDDY TRAINING (1-hour workshop):

Before pairing buddies, run training session:

1. What is buddy system? (10 min)
- Purpose, structure, expectations
- Why it matters: retention, performance, culture

2. Basic coaching skills (20 min)
- Active listening: paraphrase, reflect feelings
- Asking open questions
- Giving encouragement (specific, not generic)

3. Buddy session structure (15 min)
- Walk through 30-min format
- Practice with partner

4. Escalation protocol (10 min)
- When to escalate to leader
- How to have difficult conversations
- Emergency contacts

5. Q&A (5 min)

BUDDY PAIRING ALGORITHM:

Match based on:
1. DISC complementarity (D↔S, I↔C balance)
2. Language preference (both Vietnamese)
3. Schedule compatibility (same available time slots)
4. Experience gap (at least 2 months difference)
5. Personality: avoid pairing two extreme D-types (conflict) or two extreme S-types (no push)

BUDDY ACCOUNTABILITY FRAMEWORK:

1. WEEKLY BUDDY REPORT (Buddy fills out):
- Session completed: Yes/No
- New member's mood: Energized / Neutral / Struggling
- Key win this week: ___
- Key challenge: ___
- Action items agreed: ___
- Needs leader support: Yes/No + details

2. BUDDY SCORECARD (Monthly):
- Buddy consistency: Sessions completed / Sessions scheduled
- New member progress: Habit score trend, connect growth, first order timing
- Buddy satisfaction: New member rates buddy 1-5
- Leader assessment: Leader observes buddy's coaching quality

3. BUDDY RECOGNITION:
- Best Buddy of the Month: certificate + reward
- Impact stories: 'Thanks to Hùng's coaching, Linh recruited her first member'
- Career benefit: Buddy experience = leadership development = promotion criteria

BUDDY ESCALATION TRIGGERS:

Escalate to leader when:
- New member hasn't connected in 3+ days
- New member expressed desire to quit
- New member has personal crisis
- Buddy feels out of depth (doesn't know how to help)
- New member's habit score below 40 for 5+ days

Escalation message template:
'Leader ơi, tôi cần support. Buddy của tôi là [Name]. [Specific issue]. Tôi đã thử [what you tried]. [Name] vẫn [current state]. Cần leader support ạ.'

Action items:

4. Set up weekly buddy report system

lessons.title: Peer Accountability Framework — Cộng đồng tự điều chỉnh
lessons.objective: Build peer accountability framework để PSN tự quản mà không cần leader always present
lessons.content:
PSN mà leader phải check EVERY member EVERY day = leader là bottleneck. Peer accountability = members hold EACH OTHER accountable. Scale không giới hạn.

WHY PEER ACCOUNTABILITY WORKS:

Psychology: People care more about disappointing PEERS than disappointing a distant leader. Social pressure > top-down pressure.

Research: Teams với peer accountability perform 2.5x better than teams relying only on leader accountability.

3 LAYERS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Layer 1: SELF (Internal)
- Personal habit tracking (Droppii Points)
- Daily self-reflection: 'Did I do what I committed to?'
- Personal WHY as anchor

Layer 2: PEER (Social)
- Buddy system: 1:1 accountability
- Accountability group: 3-4 people check in daily
- PSN group: public commitment, social reinforcement

Layer 3: LEADER (Structural)
- Weekly 1:1 coaching sessions
- PIP when needed
- Recognition and consequences

Best PSNs have ALL 3 layers strong.

ACCOUNTABILITY CONTRACT:

Each member signs (verbally or written) a contract:

=== PSN ACCOUNTABILITY CONTRACT ===
Name: [Name]
PSN: [PSN name]
Date: [Date]

I commit to:
1. Daily connects: 10 minimum
2. Daily habit score: 60+ minimum
3. Weekly PSN meeting attendance: 80%+
4. 1:1 với buddy: Weekly
5. Response time: Reply within 4 hours trong PSN group
6. Honesty: Report honestly about progress and challenges

If I'm struggling, I commit to:
- Tell my buddy within 24 hours
- Attend weekly meeting even if I'm behind
- Ask for help, not hide my challenges

Accountability partners:
- Buddy: [Name]
- Accountability group: [Names]

Signed: ___ Date: ___
=========

ACCOUNTABILITY GROUPS (Triads):

Structure: 3-4 members grouped together for daily check-in
Purpose: Small group accountability — more intimate than full PSN

Daily check-in (5 min, Zalo group):
Each member posts:
- ✅ Yesterday's commitment: completed / not completed
- 🎯 Today's focus: 1 main thing
- 💬 Need help with: anything blocking them

Example accountability group chat:
Minh: '✅ Completed 15 connects. 🎯 Today: first recruit approach. 💬 Need: DM script for initial contact'
Lan: '❌ Only 5 connects yesterday — struggling with motivation. 🎯 Today: 10 connects. 💬 Need: encouragement'
Hùng: '✅ 20 connects + 1 order! 🎯 Today: help Lan with DM script'
→ This IS peer accountability in action

ACCOUNTABILITY GROUP RULES:
1. Daily check-in by 8am (non-negotiable)
2. Honesty over performance (real > impressive)
3. Support, not shame (struggling members get help, not judgment)
4. Celebrate wins (make success visible)
5. Privacy: group chat stays within the triad

CULTURE OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Building accountability culture requires:

1. LEAD BY EXAMPLE:
Leader must be most accountable person in PSN.
- Leader always completes commitments
- Leader admits mistakes publicly
- Leader shows up consistently

2. NORMALIZE STRUGGLE:
- Sharing struggles is WELCOME, not shameful
- 'I struggled this week too' builds psychological safety
- When leader shares vulnerability, others follow

3. RECOGNIZE ACCOUNTABILITY:
- Celebrate people who follow through
- 'Shoutout to Lan — committed to 10 connects every day this week and DID IT'
- Make accountability visible and admired

4. MAKE IT EASY:
- Simple check-in format (emoji + 1 line)
- Low friction: Zalo group, 1 minute to post
- Remove excuses: 'It only takes 60 seconds'

5. CONSEQUENCES (gentle but real):
- Miss 3 check-ins: buddy reaches out personally
- Miss 1 week: leader 1:1
- Miss 2 weeks: PIP conversation
- Not punitive — about caring enough to follow through

ACCOUNTABILITY METRICS:

Track these monthly:
- Daily check-in rate: ___% (target: 80%+)
- Buddy session completion: ___% (target: 90%+)
- Commitment follow-through: ___% (actions completed vs committed)
- PSN meeting attendance: ___% (target: 80%+)
- Member self-reported accountability: Survey 1-5

Action items:

2. Set up accountability group Zalo chats
3. Have each member sign accountability contract
4. Launch daily check-in routine starting this week

lessons.title: Coaching Session Practice — Full GROW Cycle
lessons.objective: Practice complete GROW coaching cycle với real team members
lessons.content:
Hôm nay là practice day. Bạn sẽ conduct a FULL GROW coaching session với một team member, từ contracting đến will, và document the entire session.

FULL GROW SESSION PRACTICE:

PREPARATION (5 min before session):
- Review member's recent performance data
- Think about 1-2 areas they might want to discuss
- Prepare your space: quiet, no interruptions, 30 min blocked
- Have GROW template ready for notes

SESSION FLOW (30 min):

Phase 0 — Contracting (3 min):
'Thanks for making time. Today we have 30 minutes. I'd like to focus on [area — let them refine it]. By the end, what would make this session valuable for you?'

Phase 1 — Goal (5 min):
'What do you want to achieve?' → Drill to specificity
'On a scale of 1-10, how committed are you?'
If < 8: 'What would make it higher?'

Phase 2 — Reality (5 min):
'Where are you now with this?' → Facts, not stories
'What have you tried?' → Past actions
'What's in your way?' → Obstacles

Phase 3 — Options (8 min):
'What are all the possible ways?' → Generate 10+
'What else?' → Push beyond first 3 ideas
Don't evaluate yet — just generate

Phase 4 — Will (7 min):
'Which option will you choose?' → Decision
'What specifically will you do?' → Action
'By when?' → Deadline
'On a scale of 1-10?' → Commitment check
'What's your first step?' → Immediate action
'When will you check in with me?' → Accountability

Closing (2 min):
'Thanks for being open today. I'm excited about what you're capable of. Let's check in on [date].'

SESSION NOTES TEMPLATE:

=== COACHING SESSION LOG ===
Session #: ___
Date: ___
Coach: [You]
Coachee: [Name]
Duration: ___ min
Topic: ___

CONTRACTING:
- Coachee's desired outcome: ___

GOAL:
- Specific goal: ___
- Commitment: ___/10
- Why this matters: ___

REALITY:
- Current state: ___
- Key obstacle: ___
- Resources available: ___

OPTIONS (Top 3):
1. ___
2. ___
3. ____

WILL:
- Chosen action: ___
- Deadline: ___
- Commitment: ___/10
- First step: ___
- Check-in date: ___

COACH OBSERVATIONS:
- What went well: ___
- Coachee's breakthrough moment: ___
- What to follow up on: ___
- DISC type observation: ___
- Area for coach improvement: ___

FOLLOW-UP CHECKLIST:
- [ ] Send follow-up message within 24 hours
- [ ] Check in on agreed date
- [ ] Review progress in next PSN meeting
- [ ] Celebrate if action completed
=========

COACHING LOG TRACKING:

Maintain a coaching log (Google Sheet or notebook):

Columns: Session # | Date | Coachee | Topic | Goal | Commitment | Action | Deadline | Follow-up | Outcome

Track:
- How many sessions per week (target: 3-5)
- Average commitment score (target: 8+/10)
- Action completion rate (target: 70%+)
- Coachee progress over time

COACHING CADENCE:

New members (Week 1-4): Daily check-in (5 min Zalo)
Developing members (Month 2-3): 2x/week coaching (20 min)
Senior members (Month 4+): 1x/week coaching (30 min)
Sub-leaders: 1x/week + leadership development focus

FOLLOW-UP SYSTEM:

After each session:

Within 1 hour:
- Send summary message: 'Great session today. Your action: [X]. Deadline: [Y].'
- Add to coaching log

Day before deadline:
- Reminder: 'Hey, just checking in. How's [action] going?'

On deadline:
- Check-in: 'Did you complete [action]? How did it go?'
- If yes: Celebrate! 'That's awesome!'
- If no: 'What happened? What do you need?' → Don't shame

If no action taken:
- Diagnose: Was goal unrealistic? Was there an obstacle? Did they forget?
- Adjust: Modify action or timeline
- Re-commit: 'What CAN you commit to this week?'

lessons.title: M8 Graduation — Coaching Ready
lessons.objective: Consolidate coaching skills và prepare for advanced leadership challenges
lessons.content:
Chúc mừng hoàn thành Module 8! Coaching là skill cần cả đời để master. M8 cho bạn foundation — phần còn lại là practice, reflection, và refinement.

M8 RECAP — CORE COACHING SKILLS:

1. COACHING vs MANAGING
- Coaching: Ask, guide, empower (70%)
- Managing: Direct, command, execute (30%)
- Balance: Know when to switch

2. GROW MODEL
- G = Goal: Specific, measurable, meaningful
- R = Reality: Facts, not stories
- O = Options: 10+ ideas, no judgment
- W = Will: Specific action, time-bound, committed
- Practice until GROW becomes automatic

3. ACTIVE LISTENING
- Level 4: Full presence, reflect, summarize
- Paraphrase, reflect feelings, clarify, summarize
- Silence: most powerful tool
- 80% listen, 20% speak

4. POWERFUL QUESTIONING
- Open questions > Closed questions
- 'What else?' technique (ask 3-5 times)
- 6 question archetypes
- Avoid: Why, Leading, Multiple, Past-focused

5. DISC-BASED COACHING
- D-type: Direct, challenge, fast
- I-type: Enthusiastic, relational, fun
- S-type: Patient, supportive, slow
- C-type: Logical, systematic, precise
- Adapt your style to THEIR needs

6. BUDDY SYSTEM v2
- 30-min weekly coaching sessions
- Mini-GROW format for new members
- Buddy training workshop (1 hour)
- Escalation protocol

7. PEER ACCOUNTABILITY
- 3 layers: Self → Peer → Leader
- Accountability groups (triads)
- Accountability contracts
- Culture of accountability through leader modeling

8. FULL SESSION PRACTICE
- 30-min GROW cycle documented
- Follow-up system: within 1 hour, day-before, deadline
- Coaching log tracking
- Cadence by member stage

COACHING MASTERY SELF-ASSESSMENT:

Rate yourself 1-5 on each:

[ ] Tôi có thể conduct full GROW session without notes
[ ] Tôi listen 80% và không interupt
[ ] Tôi generate 10+ options consistently trong Options phase
[ ] Tôi adapt coaching style based on coachee's DISC type
[ ] Tôi help coachee set SMART+ goals
[ ] Tôi separate stories from facts trong Reality phase
[ ] Tôi end every session với specific action + deadline
[ ] Tôi set up và follow up on accountability
[ ] Tôi run effective buddy sessions
[ ] Tôi build peer accountability trong PSN

Score: ___/50
40-50: Coaching mastery — ready to train other leaders
30-40: Competent coach — continue practicing, focus on weak areas
20-30: Developing coach — GROW fluency growing, keep practicing

COACHING CHALLENGES (What's next):

CHALLENGE 1: The 20-Session Challenge
- Conduct 20 coaching sessions in 30 days
- Mix: new members, developing, senior
- Document each in coaching log
- Review patterns after 20 sessions

CHALLENGE 2: The DISC Challenge
- Coach each DISC type (D, I, S, C) 3 times
- Note: what works, what doesn't
- Build DISC coaching playbook for your PSN

CHALLENGE 3: The Silence Challenge
- In next 5 sessions, practice using silence 5x per session
- Count to 5 after each deep question
- Note: What insights emerge from silence?

CHALLENGE 4: The 'What Else?' Challenge
- In next 10 sessions, ask 'What else?' minimum 3x in Options phase
- Track: How many options generated (target: 10+)

LEADER DEVELOPMENT PIPELINE:

Coaching is how you build your replacement:

Level 1: COACHEE (Current)
- Receiving coaching from you
- Developing self-awareness and skills

Level 2: PEER COACH (Next 3 months)
- Starts coaching other new members as buddy
- You supervise their coaching sessions

Level 3: GROUP LEADER (Next 6 months)
- Runs PSN meetings with your support
- Coaches their own buddy pairs
- Takes ownership of PSN segment

Level 4: PSN LEADER (Next 12 months)
- Runs entire PSN independently
- You step back to upline role
- They develop THEIR sub-leaders

Your job as leader: Develop people beyond yourself.
If every person you coach eventually coaches 3 people, your impact multiplies exponentially.

TRANSITION TO ADVANCED MODULES:

M9-M12 (Tier 3 — Advanced Leadership):
- M9: Strategic Thinking — System-level PSN strategy
- M10: Team Building — Building high-performing teams
- M11: Business Mastery — Advanced sales, negotiation, closing
- M12: Legacy Leadership — Creating lasting impact, succession planning

Prerequisites for M9:
- Completed M1-M8
- Running PSN with 10+ members
- 3+ months as PSN Leader
- 5+ members have been coached by you
